title: Two Years
description:
Two years since {name} met Daeun.

Looking at the calendar, she said, "It's been exactly two years since we first met."

Triangular kimbap, buy-one-get-one. Across the convenience store counter. That was two years ago.

A lot had changed since. Gangnam was still far, the bank balance was different, the weight of Seoul was the same — and this person was still here, beside him.

"...We're okay like this, right?" Daeun said the thing she seemed not to be asking.

choices.text: "We're okay. It means a lot, you being here." — evenly
choices.result_text:
Daeun looked at {name} for a long moment. "I know. I just like to check sometimes."

The words were plain. Proof that this thing hadn't started to shake yet.

choices.text: "Two whole years. I can't believe it either." — honest
choices.result_text:
Daeun laughed. "Same."

So this is how two years pass. Moving along in a way that's not bad at all.

choices.text: "Honestly — I'm struggling a lot lately." — first time admitting it
choices.result_text:
Daeun listened quietly. The 3 billion won, the time.

"I know. I just... want to struggle with you."

That was oddly comforting.

description_if_known.daeun_romance_started:
Over two years since they became a couple.

Same room, same dawn, same ramyeon pot.
They fought sometimes — usually when {name} got sharp about money — but come morning they rode the same subway, side by side.

"What'll we do once we reach Gangnam?" Daeun asked.
"No idea. But more than getting there — I hope this train I ride with you never stops running."

Daeun rested her head on his shoulder. Two years lived inside that weight.

title: Wedding Photo
description:
A social-media alert appeared late at night. One of Daeun's friends had posted photographs from a wedding hall in Busan. {name} scrolled without thinking, then stopped at the second image.

Daeun stood at the center of the flowers in a wedding dress. She was not a guest beside the bride. She was the bride. When he enlarged the image, the familiar narrowing of her eyes when she smiled met the unfamiliar white veil.

Two years ago, she had handed him triangle kimbap across a convenience-store counter in Seoul. Now she stood at the center of a life he did not know.

choices.text: Liked it. Genuinely glad for her.
choices.result_text:
{name} pressed the heart. The count rose by one; Daeun kept smiling in the photograph. He said, "I'm glad," under his breath and closed the app.

Once, it would have taken longer to produce those words. This time the congratulations arrived first and the ache followed. Perhaps two years had changed him that much.

The phone went dark, but the white dress lingered in his palm for a moment.

choices.text: Closed the screen. Better not to see it.
choices.result_text:
{name} scrolled past the photograph. The next post advertised impossible returns on a coin. He tried to read the figures as usual, but the words would not settle.

He closed the app and laid the phone facedown. It did not ring again for a while. Life would continue, and so would he.

Before he reopened the calculator, the dark screen belonged to no one's destination.

title: She Got There First
description:
On the commute home, a photograph arrived from Daeun: a new business card, its corners still perfectly sharp. A message followed beneath it.

"I got a job! It's a small company in Gangnam."

{name} began typing congratulations, then stopped. He had spent four years naming Gangnam as his destination.

Daeun would be the first to commute there. The news was unquestionably good, yet something heavy followed the happiness into his chest.

The train window reflected a smile that had not quite formed. Even joy for someone else could carry a piece of his own story.

choices.text: "That's great. When I get there, let's grab a cafe nearby." — happy for her
choices.result_text:
"That's wonderful. Find us a café near the office after your first day."

Her reply came at once. "I already found one. When you get here, that's our first stop. Promise." A map pin followed.

{name} studied the saved location. On the map he had climbed alone, there was now a table where two people might sit. For the first time, Gangnam looked less like a target sum than the address of a promise.

choices.text: (First thought: she's going to get there before me)
choices.result_text:
As {name} typed and erased his congratulations, the typing indicator appeared and vanished several times. Daeun sent another message first. "You must be busy. We can talk later." She seemed to have noticed.

He finally sent a brief "That's great." He could not explain why her reaching the place he had promised to take her should brush against him like defeat.

The business card was bright on the screen. Looking directly at that brightness was harder than it should have been.

description_if_known.daeun_romance_started:
Daeun found a job at a small company in Gangnam. At dinner, she offered her new business card with both hands. It still carried the smell of fresh coating.

They had been together for three years, long enough to know each other's morning faces and tired footsteps. Daeun smiled. "Looks like I reached Gangnam first, Minjun."

"Cheater." {name} laughed, but the card's edge remained against his fingertip. Daeun could build a life anywhere without him. He was grateful that someone like that still chose to stay, and a little afraid that one day the choice might change.

title: The Night Before 3 billion won
description:
The number is almost there.

Daeun set out dinner. Rolled omelette — something {name} once said he liked.

An old friend. Someone who'd held on in the same city for five years.

"Something feels different today," Daeun said.

{name} didn't answer. Tomorrow he'd know.

Five years were in this dinner.

choices.text: "We got here together. Without you I'd have quit halfway." — said it for the first time
choices.result_text:
Daeun stopped, then said, "I didn't do anything."
{name} shook his head. "No. You're the reason I didn't give up."

The two of them stayed a long while. The omelette went cold.

choices.text: Ate without words. Tomorrow's soon enough.
choices.result_text:
The egg roll was warm. Daeun was quiet too.

Maybe it was nights like this that got him all the way here. A night that needed no words.

description_if_known.daeun_married:
The number is almost there.

Daeun set out dinner. Rolled omelette. Something {name} once said he liked.

The ring on her finger still felt a little unfamiliar. He'd put it there last year.

"So tomorrow you really become a Gangnam person?" she asked, smiling.
"Yeah. Though I already feel like I have everything."

Daeun poked him with her spoon. She never could take a sweet line without squirming.

Five years — and every year still to come — all of it in this one dinner.
description_if_known.daeun_year4_close:
Numbers almost there.

Daeun had made dinner. Rolled omelette. Something {name} had once mentioned liking.

"Today feels different somehow." Daeun said.

{name} said nothing. Tomorrow would show it.

Thought of that promise from four years ago — the cafe in Gangnam, when you get there. Tomorrow, that promise could be kept.

Five years lived in this one evening.
description_if_known.daeun_romance_started:
The number is almost there.

Daeun set out dinner. Rolled omelette — something {name} once said he liked.

It had been a few months since the cafe, since 'let's go together.' These dinners had become theirs since then.

"Something feels different today," Daeun said.

{name} didn't answer. Tomorrow he'd know.

Five years were in this dinner.

title: Separate Arrivals
description:
When the light changed on Gangnam-daero, the crowd crossed all at once. Looking up at apartment lights reflected in a glass façade, {name} suddenly wondered what Daeun would say if she were here.

The voice that had offered him triangle kimbap across a convenience-store counter five years ago. The white dress in a Busan wedding photograph.

The time between belonged to each of them without explanation. Daeun was probably sharing a different dinner with someone else now.

The crossing signal ended. {name} stepped into the street half a beat after everyone else.

choices.text: Each got there. Glad she's okay.
choices.result_text:
They had simply arrived in different places. His road led here; Daeun's continued somewhere beyond a screen. Neither was wrong because they no longer crossed.

{name} offered one more belated congratulations in his mind. He hoped she was well. This time he attached no story about himself to the sentence.

As he walked beyond the signal, the apartment lights disappeared behind the buildings.

choices.text: Thought about reaching out for a second, then didn't.
choices.result_text:
{name} found Daeun's name in his contacts. Her profile photograph had changed several times since the wedding. He typed, "How have you been?" and erased it.

A greeting sent while looking at Gangnam might arrive as a request to be admired. More than that, he no longer knew whether this was a door he had the right to open.

He pocketed the phone and stood alone. For a moment, the unsent sentence had weight inside his coat.

title: Today's Seoul
description:
Daeun had been commuting to her Gangnam office for two months. The alley photographs she sent at lunch now contained shops {name} recognized. That day, a window seat in a café arrived with a message.

"When are you coming to Gangnam, Minjun? I found a café near work."

Four of the five years were gone, and the goal remained some distance away. Once, her words would have touched urgency first.

Instead, {name} smiled at the empty chair across from the camera. Knowing someone had gone ahead and saved a place made Seoul feel less far away today.

description_if_known.jiyeon_respectfully_distanced:
Daeun had been commuting to her Gangnam office for two months. That day, a photograph of a café window seat arrived with a message. "When are you coming to Gangnam, Minjun? I found a café near work."

{name} paused before replying. When Jiyeon visited Seoul the month before, he had told her there was someone in his life. Daeun knew nothing about that difficult conversation.

The chair across from the camera was empty. For the first time, he could see the shape of the choice he had never described. He sent Daeun a smile and wrote the promise without hesitation.

choices.text: "Of course. The moment I get there." — affirm the promise
choices.result_text:
"Of course. The day I get there, we go."

Daeun sent another photograph, pointing at the chair across from her cup. "Then I'll save this seat." Both knew a café chair could not be held that long, yet the sentence felt natural.

{name} pocketed the phone and walked on. Somewhere he had not reached, it felt as though one chair already belonged to him.

choices.text: "Let's talk about it then. It's still far away." — answer honestly
choices.result_text:
"Let's talk when I get there. It still feels too far away."

Daeun replied after a pause. "Okay. Just don't spend too long calculating by yourself." It was neither a promise to wait nor an attempt to hurry him.

{name} did not save the café photograph. The empty window seat remained in his mind anyway.
